summary: Masaaki Noni worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Gadjin Nagao and held posts at Ryukoku University, serving as assistant professor (attested 2003) and later as professor (attested 2013–2014).

Masaaki Sugiyama (1952–2019) worked in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held a post at Kyoto Women's University (~1983–1992).
Masaaki Tsuchiya (b. 1960) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University (~1979–1984) and held a post at Senshu University around 1995.

Masaharu Anesaki (1873–1949) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo and Kiel under scholars including Tetsujiro Inoue, Friedrich Max Müller, and Paul Deussen, later serving as professor (from 1904) and library director at the University of Tokyo.

Masaharu Imai (b. 1942), a specialist in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology, earned his doctorate at Tokyo University of Education in 1977. He taught at Ibaraki University (1977) and became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba in 2006.

Masahide Mori (b. 1962) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Nagoya University and SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later holding positions at Nagoya University, Koyasan University, and Kanazawa University.
Masahiro Asada (b. 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University (~1964–1973), where he later served as an assistant professor (~1985–1991).
Masahiro Inami (b. 1960) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Hiroshima University and held teaching posts at Tokyo Gakugei University (attested ~1993 and ~2008).

Masahiro Kusunoki (1921–2009) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1947–1953) and served there as chair professor of religious studies and the history of religion (~1974–1985).

Masahiro Shimoda (b. 1957) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Delhi. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and joined Musashino University in 2023.
Masahiro Takano (b. 1960) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also served as a librarian (attested 1995).

Masakatsu Fujita (b. 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1968–1978), where he later headed the Department of the History of Japanese Philosophy (~2001–2014).

Masakazu Tanaka (b. 1955) works in religious studies. He studied at Tohoku University and earned his Ph.D. from the London School of Economics, later serving as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and vice president at the Professional Institute of International Fashion.

Masako Keta (b. 1953) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi and held posts at Kanazawa University before serving as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).
Masamichi Asukai (1934–2000) was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at Kyoto University (~1954–1961) and later held an academic post there (~1968–1998).

Masamichi Ichigo (b. 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin Nagao, later holding posts at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Helmut Krasser in 2006.

Masanori Nakagawa works in the field of Buddhist studies. He held posts as a lecturer (attested 1991) and assistant professor in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Masanori Shono specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe (1915–2006) specialized in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto, Union Theological Seminary, and Columbia, and held professorships at Kyoto Women's University, Otani University, Kyoto University, and Nara University.
